findings.F1: On down days the next-day excess return grows with the day's high-low range measured in 60-day standard deviations of daily returns: −0.184 % (t −1.08, 706 days) in the narrowest fifth, rising through +0.069 % and +0.140 % to +0.882 % (t 3.41, day-clustered, 1648 cases on 596 days) in the widest fifth. On up days the same widest fifth gives −0.324 % (t −1.43), so the effect belongs to falls.
findings.F2: The rebound after falls (latest day below −0.5 standard deviations) is graded by the coin's 10-day volatility against its 60-day volatility: −0.167 % (t −0.79, 580 days) when the last 10 days are calmer, +0.389 % (t 1.96, 668 days) when they are about the same, and +0.947 % (t 3.28, 578 days) when they are hotter.
findings.F3: Falls taken when the coin's 60-day volatility is in its own highest third rebound +0.861 % the next day (t 2.53, 521 days), against +0.152 % and +0.199 % in the lower two thirds. The rebound is positive in all six coins (+0.58 % BTC to +1.37 % XMR) and in every year with data except 2022 (−0.14 %).
findings.F4: Sorting down days by their raw percentage fall, with no volatility scaling, gives the same grading: +0.690 % (t 2.42, 614 days) after the largest fifth of falls and +0.292 % after the next, down to −0.223 % and −0.077 % after the smallest. The days with the largest falls also cluster on fewer calendar days (614 against about 1100), which points to market-wide volatile episodes.
findings.F5: Down days that close in the lowest fifth of their high-low range rise +0.349 % the next day (t 2.24, 1252 days), against −0.217 % and −0.785 % for down days closing in the upper fifths. This is weaker than F1 to F3 given the number of angles looked at.
findings.F6: The tested signal's edge (+0.19 % unusual move per case, about 1.0 times the 0.19 % cost) is concentrated: falls on wide-range days, on volatility-heating days or in high-volatility thirds carry an unusual next-day move of about +0.86 % to +0.95 %, roughly 4.5 to 5 times the cost of a trade.
findings.F7: After a coin's 10-day return falls to its lowest tenth in 60-day volatility units, the 5-day excess return is +1.70 %, but with t 1.48 on 108 days it cannot be told from chance. The same holds for signal-day weekday effects (Friday +0.305 %, Wednesday −0.299 %, not day-clustered and one of many angles), which I do not use.

ideas.idea: The wider a coin's high-low range on a day it closes down, measured against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 60 days, the more the coin rises over the next 1 day.
ideas.consequence: A trader buying a fall should favour falls made on wide, violent days and refuse the rebound trade after narrow, quiet down days.
ideas.name: wide-range fall next-day rebound

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's fall on its latest day, the more it rises over the next 1 day, and this rebound is larger the higher the standard deviation of the coin's daily returns over the past 10 days stands against that over the past 60 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader should expect a dip to rebound strongly when the coin's volatility is heating up, and expect no rebound when the coin has recently been calmer than usual.
ideas.name: rebound grows as volatility heats

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's fall on its latest day, the more it rises over the next 1 day, and this rebound is larger the higher the coin's 60-day standard deviation of daily returns stands against its own past values.
ideas.consequence: A trader should size dip-buying up in the coin's high-volatility periods, where the next-day rebound is several times the cost of a trade, and treat dips in calm periods as no edge.
ideas.name: high-volatility dip rebound
